sources.citation: Wrembel, Magdalena (2009). On Hearing Colours — Cross-Modal Associations in Vowel Perception in a Non-Synaesthetic Population. Poznań Studies in Contemporary Linguistics 45. Versita. pp. 595-612.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Mislinked to prov1243. The article is a perception experiment in which 90 Polish learners of English matched 12 English vowel stimuli (isolated and in CVC context) to 11 basic colours; it concerns English vowels and synaesthesia-like cross-modal mapping, not Providencia Sign Language or any sign language, and contains no word-stress statement (a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence/tone/prosody/sign/deaf/Providencia: only 'tonality axis', 'pure tones', 'low pitch tones' in the synaesthesia literature review). sources.note: Describes British Sign Language (BSL), not Providencia Sign Language; 'Providence' occurs only in a reference (Brown University Press, Providence, Rhode Island) and 'prosodic' only in the title of Brentari 1999 in the reference list. Attempt 1 at the listed ScienceDirect PDF URL could not be reached by automated download bot page; attempt 2 downloaded the same CC BY 3.0 article from Europe PMC (PMC2278232). Read: abstract, introduction, materials and methods, discussion; full-text search for stress/accent/prosod/suprasegment/tone/Providen/Colombia.

sources.citation: Butcher, Andrew and Fletcher, Janet and Stoakes, Hywel and Tabain, Marija (2012). Australian phonologies and aborginal hearing: Is there a link?.
sources.note: Mislinked to prov1243. The e-lecture page (seminar abstract + presenter bio; the video sat in a JCU Digital Media Flash jwplayer and is not archived) concerns otitis-media hearing loss and the sound systems of Australian Aboriginal spoken languages (Yolngu Matha, Pitjantjatjara, Australian Aboriginal English long-term average spectra, place-of-articulation contrasts). No mention of any sign language, Providencia, or word stress/accent/prosody (a full-text search for stress/accent: no hits). Attempts: (1) listed JCU URL with browser UA -> not reachable by automated download an automated-access…

sources.citation: Omardeen, Rehana. 2022 [online 2023]. Providence Island Sign Language in Interaction. PhD dissertation, Georg-August-Universität Göttingen. 236 pp. DOI 10.53846/goediss-10243, hdl 11858/15035.
sources.note: Nothing. No phonology or prosody chapter (chapters: introduction; sampling signers; initial person reference; other-initiated repair; discussion). Ch.2 §2.2 'Linguistic Research' (pp.40-42) reviews all prior PISL work as sociolinguistic plus basic lexical elicitation; full-text search for stress/prosod/accent/phonolog/suprasegment finds only incidental mentions of a 'prosodic pause' separating alternatives in repair sequences.
sources.venue: Providence Island Sign Language in Interaction
